modes.match: (?i)(not enough free disk space|no space left on device|partition .* too full)
modes.meaning: The transaction cannot retain both old and new package archives.
modes.response: Below 6 GiB free on / the look fails with this case. The repair runs sudo paccache -rk2 (keeps the two newest cached versions of each package), then the machine is looked at again; up to three such rounds per run. If / is still below 6 GiB, the run stops before any update, with the fix below. The same limit and the same cleanup apply to the update from the screen and to the unattended run.

modes.meaning: A package was replaced, renamed or split while its conflicting predecessor remains installed.
modes.response: Name both packages (the fix prints the conflict lines), check with pacman -Qi <name> which one is the old one and where it came from, then run sudo pacman -Syu without --noconfirm: pacman asks whether to remove the old one, so the exact removal is visible before it happens.

modes.meaning: A mirror database advertised a package artifact that the same mirror no longer serves.
modes.response: Let pacman try the next mirror; if all mirrors fail, refresh mirror state once and rerun the unchanged transaction.

modes.match: (?i)(no tracking information|no upstream branch|not currently on a branch)
modes.meaning: The AUR build cache is a broken git checkout, not a package failure.
modes.response: Quarantine only that package cache and fetch a clean copy once. The fix opens the last run's log, where yay names the package; delete that folder under ~/.cache/yay, then run yay -Sua.

modes.match: (?i)(error downloading sources: .*?/yay/[^\s]+|failed to parse .*\.SRCINFO:.*no such file)
modes.meaning: yay named one of its cache directories, but that directory has no PKGBUILD to parse.
modes.response: Verify the named path is a direct non-symlink yay cache child, quarantine it reversibly, then fetch it cleanly once.

modes.match: (?i)(is not a clone of|does not match.*url|remote.*mismatch)
modes.meaning: makepkg accepts source repositories by configured origin URL as well as object integrity.
modes.response: Restore the PKGBUILD-declared origin URL after an alternate transport fetch; then verify objects.

modes.meaning: The PKGBUILD source protocol helper is missing before source preparation.
modes.response: Install the declared git-lfs make dependency and retry source preparation once.

modes.match: (?i)(sudo: a password is required|incorrect password attempts|authentication is required)
modes.meaning: A long AUR build outlived terminal-scoped sudo authentication.
modes.response: Use pkexec as yay's sudo command or keep authentication alive explicitly; never place a password in argv or logs.
modes.fix: sh -c 'f=$(mktemp) && arch-update auto --sudoers > "$f" && visudo -cf "$f" && sudo install -m 0440 "$f" /etc/sudoers.d/zzz-arch-update-auto; rm -f "$f"'

modes.meaning: Installing split outputs one by one can repeatedly prepare the same large source tree.
modes.response: Build the pkgbase once and install only the names already present on the machine in one pacman -U transaction.

modes.meaning: The PKGBUILD was fetched correctly but its build layer failed; retrying the package manager unchanged cannot repair source or compiler state.
modes.response: Capture the first compiler error, keep the failed pkgbase isolated, and continue only independent packages.

modes.match: (?i)(dkms install.*exited [1-9]|bad return status for module build|Error! Bad return status)
modes.meaning: The kernel package installed, but at least one out-of-tree module did not build for that kernel.
modes.response: List DKMS status per installed kernel and distinguish required GPU/storage modules from optional peripherals before reboot.

modes.meaning: A mixed repo/AUR Hyprland chain crossed a shared-library SONAME boundary.
modes.response: Treat Hyprland, hyprutils, hyprlang, hyprgraphics, aquamarine and the portal as one ABI unit before reboot.

modes.match: running kernel module directory is missing
modes.meaning: The old running kernel was replaced on disk; new module loads wait for reboot.
modes.response: Do not rebuild the deleted old tree. Verify the new kernel, DKMS and initramfs, then mark reboot required.

modes.meaning: Package defaults changed but local configuration remains authoritative.
modes.response: Inventory and diff each file; never merge all pacnew files blindly.

modes.meaning: The update introduced a unit failure relative to the preflight baseline.
modes.response: Report only the set difference from the baseline and inspect that unit's current journal.

modes.meaning: The kernel package database and its bootable vmlinuz/initramfs surface disagree.
modes.response: Regenerate the affected preset and stop before reboot if either artifact remains absent or empty.

modes.match: bootloader does not reference selected kernel
modes.meaning: Kernel files exist but the boot menu cannot select the desired profile.
modes.response: Regenerate the detected bootloader configuration and verify the selected vmlinuz path appears.

modes.meaning: Another package manager holds the pacman database, or died holding it.
modes.response: Wait for it; never remove the lock while its owner may be alive.

modes.match: (?i)(could not resolve host|temporary failure in name resolution)
modes.meaning: Names do not resolve, so no mirror can be reached.
modes.response: Flush the resolver cache and wait; never rewrite resolver configuration.

modes.meaning: A locally built program no longer starts because the libraries it was built against moved.
modes.response: Rebuild that package against the libraries installed now. The check above names it; the fix lists the locally built packages, then yay -S --rebuild <name>.

modes.meaning: AUR did not say how old its packages are, so none of them is trusted this run.
modes.response: Wait and ask again; build nothing until it answers.

modes.meaning: pacman -Dk found the local package database inconsistent.
modes.response: Stop before any transaction and read the report by hand.

modes.meaning: The pre-update record has nowhere to land.
modes.response: Mount or fix the keep directory; no update runs without its record.

modes.meaning: One of the owner's own conditions said no.
modes.response: Whatever that condition's command prints is the reason.

modes.meaning: This machine has no auto config, so nothing is assumed safe.
modes.response: Write the config once.

modes.meaning: sudo -n does not work, or the run was started as root.
modes.response: Install the exact sudoers rules; run as the desktop user.
modes.fix: sh -c 'f=$(mktemp) && arch-update auto --sudoers > "$f" && visudo -cf "$f" && sudo install -m 0440 "$f" /etc/sudoers.d/zzz-arch-update-auto; rm -f "$f"'

modes.meaning: The run was asked to stop between two stores.
modes.response: The run was stopped (Ctrl-C or a signal) and nothing new was started. Open arch-update and answer yes again.
